source_text: Sed ut revertamur, unde digressi sumus, liquerat ab eo, quem fateremur verum Deum, nihil in iudicio posse fieri, quod iustitiae repugnaret, ac per hoc nec pro alienis peccatis quosquam reos teneri atque ideo nascentium innocentiam nequaquam damnari ob iniquitatem parentum, quia iniustum esset, ut reatus per semina traderetur.
pass_a_gloss: But that we may return from where we have digressed, it had become liquid that by him whom we would confess the true God nothing can be done in judgment which would fight against justice, and through this neither can anyone be held defendants for others' sins, and therefore the innocence of those being born is by no means condemned for the injustice of parents, because it would be unjust that guilt be handed over through seeds.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: But to return to the point from which we digressed: it had become clear that the one we acknowledge as the true God can do nothing in judgment that conflicts with justice. Consequently, no one can be held guilty for another’s sins, and so the innocence of newborn children cannot possibly be condemned for their parents’ wrongdoing, since it would be unjust for guilt to pass through reproductive seed.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
